newsitem.title: USA: Seagate shares rise on strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Seagate shares rise on strong earnings.

text.p: Shares of Seagate Technology Inc rose Wednesday, bouyed by better-than-expected third quarter earnings on Tuesday.

Shares of the Scotts Valley, Calif.-based company were 7/8 higher at 52-3/8 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. On Tuesday Seagate posted earnings per share of $1.01, after charges, beating analysts' estimates of $0.88 a share, according to First Call.
"I think out of all the public disk drive companies Seagate is still the premier company," said Patrick Tenney, an analyst at Robertson Stephens & Co.
Tenney raised earnings per share estimates for Seagate to $3.56 a share from $3.17 for fiscal 1997 and to $4.68 from $4.09 for 1998.
"Demand was strong and the company believes that demand is still strong," he said. "Seagate is still number one in terms of market share ... but where Seagate really dominates is the high end."
Tenney estimated that Seagate has about 60 percent market share of the high-end of the disk drive market for servers.
Seagate earnings were boosted by better high-end unit sales as well as higher gross margins from efficiencies gained through the acquisition of Conner Peripherals.

Paul Weinstein, analyst at PaineWebber Inc also raised his estimates after the strong earnings. Weinstein raised earnings per share estimates for Seagate to $3.57 a share from $3.22 for fiscal 1997 and to $4.58 from $4.30 for 1998.
Weinstein said that due to easy comparisons earnings per share should grow at over 100 per share for the next two quarters but then drop to single digits in early 1998.
On Tuesday Seagate reported third quarter earnings of $257 milion, or $1.01 a share, on record revenues of $2.5 billion. In the year-ago quarter the company.
Results for the quarter included acquisition related charges of $24.3 million, without the charges earnings per share would have been $1.07.
In the comparable year-ago quarter Seagate lost $157 million, or $0.78 a share, on revenues of $2.09 billion. Without charges taken in that quarter earnings per share would have been $0.35.
